cemc-fryer-2006-01a.title: Balance around 84
cemc-fryer-2006-01a.body:
Differences from $84$: $+10, +9, 0, -3, -10, -1, -5$. They add to $19 - 19 = 0$, so the average is $84$.

**Answer: 84**

cemc-fryer-2006-01b.title: French mark of 100
cemc-fryer-2006-01b.body:
The best case is $100$ in French: $\frac{588 + 100}{8} = \frac{688}{8} = 86$.

**Answer: 86**

cemc-fryer-2006-01b.title: Share the extra
cemc-fryer-2006-01b.body:
A $100$ is $16$ above her current average of $84$; shared over $8$ courses it raises the average by $2$, to $86$.

**Answer: 86**

cemc-fryer-2006-01c.title: Use totals
cemc-fryer-2006-01c.body:
Eight courses averaging $85$ total $8 \times 85 = 680$. The first seven total $588$, so French is $680 - 588 = 92$.

**Answer: 92**

cemc-fryer-2006-01c.title: Halfway
cemc-fryer-2006-01c.body:
A French mark of $84$ keeps the average at $84$; a mark of $100$ gives $86$. The average changes evenly with the mark, so an average of $85$ (halfway) needs a mark halfway between $84$ and $100$: $92$.

**Answer: 92**

cemc-fryer-2006-02a.title: Odd squares
cemc-fryer-2006-02a.body:
The layers are the squares of the odd numbers $1, 3, 5, 7$: $1 + 9 + 25 + 49 = 84$.

**Answer: 84 cubes**

cemc-fryer-2006-02b.title: Look from above and from the sides
cemc-fryer-2006-02b.body:
From above you see a full $7 \times 7$ square of top faces (from all layers): $49$. From each of the four sides you see $1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16$ faces: $64$ in total. Bottom faces are hidden by the table. Total $49 + 64 = 113$.

**Answer: 113**

cemc-fryer-2006-02b.title: Cube by cube
cemc-fryer-2006-02b.body:
Top cube: $5$ faces. In each of the other layers, the $4$ corner cubes show $3$ faces each ($12$), and edge (non-corner) cubes show $2$: the $3 \times 3$ layer has $4$ of them ($8$ faces), the $5 \times 5$ layer $12$ ($24$), the $7 \times 7$ layer $20$ ($40$). Total $5 + (12 + 8) + (12 + 24) + (12 + 40) = 113$.

**Answer: 113**

cemc-fryer-2006-02c.title: Best faces for each kind of cube
cemc-fryer-2006-02c.body:
- **Top cube** (5 visible faces): hide the $1$; visible $2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20$.
- **Corner cubes** (3 visible faces: top and two sides; $12$ of them): show $4, 5, 6$, which meet at a corner since no two of them are opposite. Each gives $15$: total $180$.
- **Edge cubes** (2 visible faces: top and one side; $4 + 12 + 20 = 36$ of them): show $5$ and $6$, which share an edge. Each gives $11$: total $396$.
- Hidden cubes contribute nothing.

Maximum total: $20 + 180 + 396 = 596$.

**Answer: 596**

cemc-fryer-2006-02c.title: Top view plus side views
cemc-fryer-2006-02c.body:
Put a $6$ on top of every cube: the $49$ top faces give $294$. The top cube also shows $2, 3, 4, 5$ on its sides: $14$. The other side faces ($4(3 + 5 + 7) = 60$) would ideally all be $5$, giving $300$, but each of the $12$ corner cubes shows two side faces and has only one $5$, so one of those becomes a $4$ ($4, 5, 6$ meet at a vertex): subtract $12$.

Total: $294 + 14 + 300 - 12 = 596$.

**Answer: 596**

cemc-fryer-2006-03a.title: Pythagoras
cemc-fryer-2006-03a.body:
In isosceles $\triangle AOB$ ($AO = OB$), the perpendicular from $O$ bisects $AB$, so $AP = 6$. Then $OP = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$.

**Answer: 8**

cemc-fryer-2006-03a.title: 3-4-5 triangle
cemc-fryer-2006-03a.body:
$\triangle AOP$ has hypotenuse $10$ and leg $6$: it is a $6$–$8$–$10$ triangle (twice $3$–$4$–$5$), so $OP = 8$.

**Answer: 8**

cemc-fryer-2006-03b.title: Three congruent triangles
cemc-fryer-2006-03b.body:
Each triangle has base $12$ and height $8$, area $\frac12 \cdot 12 \cdot 8 = 48$. Three of them: $144$.

**Answer: 144**

cemc-fryer-2006-03b.title: Trapezoid formula
cemc-fryer-2006-03b.body:
Parallel sides $AB = 12$ and $DC = DO + OC = 24$, height $OP = 8$: area $\frac12 (12 + 24)(8) = 144$.

**Answer: 144**

cemc-fryer-2006-03c.title: Find XY
cemc-fryer-2006-03c.body:
$XY$ joins the midpoints of the legs, so it is parallel to the bases, halfway up: each small trapezoid has height $4$. The midline of a trapezoid is the average of the bases: $XY = \frac{12 + 24}{2} = 18$.

- $ABYX$: $\frac12(12 + 18)(4) = 60$.
- $XYCD$: $\frac12(18 + 24)(4) = 84$.

Ratio $60 : 84 = 5 : 7$.

**Answer: $5 : 7$**

cemc-fryer-2006-03c.title: Twelve small triangles
cemc-fryer-2006-03c.body:
Join the midpoints of all the sides of the three big triangles. Each big triangle splits into $4$ congruent small triangles (sides $5, 5, 6$), so the trapezoid is made of $12$ equal small triangles. The line $XY$ passes through these midpoints; above it lie $5$ small triangles and below it $7$. So the ratio of areas is $5 : 7$.

**Answer: $5 : 7$**

cemc-fryer-2006-04a.title: Count those with a 7
cemc-fryer-2006-04a.body:
Ending in $7$: $7, 17, \dots, 97$ ($10$ numbers). Tens digit $7$: $70, \dots, 79$ ($10$). $77$ is in both, so $19$ numbers contain a $7$. Answer: $100 - 19 = 81$.

**Answer: 81**

cemc-fryer-2006-04a.title: Two-digit strings
cemc-fryer-2006-04a.body:
Replace $100$ by $0$ (neither has a $7$) and write $0$–$99$ as $00$–$99$. Each digit has $9$ choices other than $7$: $9 \times 9 = 81$.

**Answer: 81**

cemc-fryer-2006-04b.title: Four-digit strings
cemc-fryer-2006-04b.body:
Replace $2000$ by $0000$ (neither contains $7$) and count $0000$–$1999$: the first digit is $0$ or $1$ ($2$ choices), and each of the other three digits has $9$ choices. Total $2 \times 9^3 = 1458$.

**Answer: 1458**

cemc-fryer-2006-04b.title: Blocks of 100
cemc-fryer-2006-04b.body:
Each block of $100$ ($1$–$100$, $101$–$200$, ...) whose hundreds digit isn't $7$ and doesn't end at a number like $700$ contains $81$ such numbers. Blocks $601$–$700$ and $1601$–$1700$ have $80$ (since $700$, $1700$ contain $7$); blocks $701$–$800$ and $1701$–$1800$ have only $1$ ($800$, $1800$). The other $16$ blocks have $81$. Total $16 \cdot 81 + 2 \cdot 80 + 2 \cdot 1 = 1458$.

**Answer: 1458**

cemc-fryer-2006-04c.title: Blocks of 100
cemc-fryer-2006-04c.body:
From $1$ to $100$ the numbers containing a $7$ are $7, 17, \dots, 67, 70, \dots, 79, 87, 97$, with sum $1188$, so the good numbers sum to $5050 - 1188 = 3862$ ($81$ numbers).

A block $100k + 1$ to $100k + 100$ (hundreds digit not $7$) has the same $81$ numbers shifted by $100k$: sum $3862 + 8100k$. Adjust where $7$ appears: blocks ending in $700$ or $1700$ lose that number, and the blocks $701$–$800$, $1701$–$1800$ contain only $800$, $1800$. Summing the $18$ full blocks for $k \in \{0,\dots,6, 8,\dots,16, 18, 19\}$, the corrections, and $2001$–$2006$:
$$18(3862) + 8100(166) - 700 - 1700 + 800 + 1800 + 12\,021 = 1\,426\,337.$$

**Answer: 1 426 337**
